classification.reason: Russia remains India's largest single source of major arms imports and discounted crude oil (since Western sanctions redirected Russian oil eastward). India also values Russia as a hedge against overdependence on the US.
classification.source: SIPRI arms transfer data; multiple India-Russia oil trade reports 2022-2026

strategic_issues: India balances its Russia ties against its deepening US/Quad partnership
Western sanctions on Russia complicate payment and shipping for Indian buyers
trade_dependencies: India is a major buyer of discounted Russian crude oil since 2022
India remains reliant on Russian-origin spare parts for a large share of its legacy military hardware

energy_relationship.notes: Russia became one of India's top crude oil suppliers after 2022 due to discounted pricing following Western sanctions

military_relationship.notes: Russia remains India's largest cumulative arms supplier historically, though India has diversified toward France, the US, and Israel in recent years

diplomatic_relationship.notes: Both are members of BRICS and SCO; India has avoided formally condemning Russia over Ukraine, preferring a neutral, interest-based stance

areas_of_cooperation: Defence equipment and co-production (e.g. BrahMos missile, licensed manufacturing)
deescalation_factors: Both sides have strong incentives to keep this relationship stable regardless of India's other partnerships

_meta.data_quality: demo/approximate baseline with sourced general trend
